evidence: Wikipedia's article on 'Kid A' names Can among its influences, alongside the Warp artists, jazz and Björk.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: 'Halleluhwah' is eighteen minutes on one tight drum and bass groove that never changes. 'The National Anthem' is built the same way, on one repeated, distorted bass riff, with free-jazz horns piling up on top until it nearly collapses. Listen to the bass line and count how long it stays the same.

explanation: Can were a German band from the late 1960s and 1970s who played one groove for a very long time. Radiohead named them as an influence on 'Kid A', and what they took was Can's method: a locked, repeating groove that the other players work against. It is Can's second route into British rock on this map, after Public Image Ltd.
